predecessors.note: 19 September 855, Treaty of Prüm: Lothair I divides Middle Francia between his three sons; Charles, the youngest, receives Lower Burgundy with Provence.

land.text: Provence and the Rhône-Saône lands; Rudolph II of Upper Burgundy receives them from Hugh of Italy in 933 and unites the two Burgundies

successors.note: Viennois and Lyonnais pass to Rudolph II already in 931; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Arles (936) is the union of the two Burgundian shapes.

capitals.name: Vienne
capitals.note: Louis the Blind page: 'Louis returned to Vienne, his capital' (after 905); the Boso and Charles of Provence pages name no capital; Hugh 'later moved the capital to Arles' (undated, 4.63 E 43.68 N). Vienne is used for the whole span; no capital is named for 855-863. Kingdom of Arles page (opened 2026-10-24): Boso's kingdom was 'centered at Vienne and Arles' (879); the page does not say the capital moved from Vienne to Arles, does not date a move by Hugh (the Hugh of Italy page: 'He moved the capital to his family's chief seat of Arles', undated) and names no capital for Charles of Provence's domain.

rulers.name: Charles of Provence
rulers.note: Reign 23 September 855 to January 863 (infobox); 25 January 863 in the lead; Count Girart de Roussillon was regent.

rulers.name: Boso of Provence
rulers.note: Elected king at the Synod of Mantaille, 15 October 879; died 11 January 887 (infobox).

rulers.name: Louis the Blind
rulers.note: Confirmed in Provence by Charles the Fat in May 887; proclaimed king at Valence, August 890; blinded 21 July 905 and left Hugh of Arles as the real ruler by 911; died 5 June 928.

rulers.name: Hugh of Arles (Hugh of Italy)
rulers.title: king of Italy, ruling Provence de facto
rulers.note: 'After Louis the Blind died, Hugh annexed the kingdom to Italy de facto'; he cedes it to Rudolph II in 933.

correction.text: Charles of Provence's kingdom: 'Lower Burgundy with Provence' (Cliopatria's 860 shape minus the Lotharingian part it keeps from 866, but with the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble, which Lothair received on his death)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Lower Burgundy begins in 860, but the page gives the Treaty of Prüm of 19 September 855 ('Charles ... received Lower Burgundy with Provence'). The shape drawn is the southern part of Cliopatria's 860 polygon; the 860 polygon also holds the northern Lotharingian lands (see lower-burgundy_860). The page gives no area or county list for Charles. Reviewer's repair, 2026-10-24: Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble lie inside Cliopatria's 866 polygon (Lothair II's kingdom) and were therefore subtracted with it, but they were Charles's until his death ('Lothair received the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble'); the Lyonnais, Vienne (60 km) and Grenoble (60 km) are put back where they lie inside the 860 polygon: 260 cells instead of 211 (12 cells of the Lyonnais region fall outside Cliopatria's 860 polygon, are West Frankish in its West Franks shapes and are not added).

minus.text: Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble, which Lothair received on Charles's death
the part of the 866 polygon that is Lothair II's kingdom and not Charles's

correction.text: Charles of Provence's kingdom: 'Lower Burgundy with Provence' (Cliopatria's 860 shape minus the Lotharingian part it keeps from 866, but with the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble, which Lothair received on his death)

keyframe_review.note: 860-865, 893 cells (209,032 km2). Two kingdoms in one polygon: the southern 211 cells are Charles of Provence's realm without Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble, which the 866 polygon holds; they are put back (260 cells); the northern part (Belgium, the Netherlands, the Rhineland, bbox to 52.9 N) is Lothair II's Lotharingia, which Cliopatria also draws as 'Lower Burgundy' 866-869. Correct to Charles's realm only, and only to January 863: 'when Charles died, his elder brother Louis also claimed Provence'; Lothair received Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble, Louis Arles, Aix and Embrun, so the state holds nothing 863-878 (ledger 863). Charles of Provence page: on his death 'Lothair received the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble', Louis those of Arles, Aix and Embrun; the ledger's 863 losses now remove land the keyframes hold.

correction.text: empty: Lower Burgundy holds no land from 863 to 878 ('his realm was divided between his brothers')

keyframe_review.note: 866-869, 684 cells. After Charles's death in January 863 the kingdom was divided between his brothers, so there is no Lower Burgundy in 866-869; this polygon is Lothair II's Lotharingia (Belgium, Netherlands, Lorraine, bbox 3.4-8.3 E, 43.5-52.9 N), which belongs to a Lotharingia dossier (counterparts_needing_dossiers) and, after Meerssen (August 870), to West and East Francia. Empty here.

union.text: Boso's realm as it stood from Mantaille
Mâcon and the northern parts of Boso's realm

correction.text: Boso's realm of October 1879 including Mâcon and the north, which the brothers took after March 880

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 879 only: Cliopatria's Lower Burgundy begins in 880, after the brothers' campaign, so Boso's realm of 15 October 879 (the revival of the state after the gap of 863-878) has no shape and Mâcon, which 'they took' in 880, is a shape no keyframe gave him (Cliopatria's 880 polygon holds 2 of the 35 Saône-et-Loire cells). The realm is Cliopatria's 880 shape plus Saône-et-Loire; the page names Mâcon only (the Boso page's list of provinces does not name Mâcon; its sentence on 880 does, as part of Boso's realm) and the region is the Saône-et-Loire reading. West Francia loses the same land in its west-franks_879 keyframe.

880-881, 301 cells (72,811 km2); the infobox of the Lower Burgundy page gives no area. Boso's kingdom 'comprised the ecclesiastical provinces of Arles, Aix, Vienne, and Lyon (without Langres), probably Besançon, and the dioceses of Tarentaise, Uzès and Viviers'; the polygon (3.9-7.6 E, 43.1-46.9 N) fits that. From October 879 to March 1880 the realm also held the northern parts that the Carolingians took in March 880 (ledger). Adjusted by 2 cells: Cliopatria's polygon holds 2 of the 35 Saône-et-Loire cells, which West Francia holds in its 880 keyframe (the Boso page: 'They took Mâcon and the northern parts of Boso's realm', after the Amiens division of March 880); removed so that the two dossiers do not claim them both.

correction.text: Boso's realm after the brothers took Mâcon and the north: Cliopatria's 880 shape without Saône-et-Loire (2 of its 301 cells)

keyframe_review.note: 882-883, 20 cells: 'Boso was restricted to the county of Vienne' after the siege of August-September 882, when Richard the Justiciar took the city. The page dates only the city's fall (Boso 'again besieged at Vienne by his brother, who took the city in September') and gives the sentence 'Boso never regained much of his realm and was restricted to the county of Vienne' with no year; the county of Vienne is kept as Boso's shape in 882-886 although Richard held the city itself from September 882.
884-886, 19 cells: the county of Vienne, all that remained to Boso (d. January 887).

887, 295 cells: 'In May, Ermengard traveled to Charles' court with Louis, and received confirmation of family estates'; Charles the Fat confirmed Louis in Provence, restoring the realm to roughly Boso's 880 extent.
888-895, 294 cells: Louis the Blind's Provence and Lower Burgundy; proclaimed king at the Diet of Valence in August 890 and did homage to Arnulf in 894.
896-899, 295 cells: unchanged realm (the one-cell difference from 888 is Lyonnais; no event on any opened page).

911-921, 295 cells: after 905 the blinded Louis 'returned to Vienne, his capital'; 'by 911 most of the royal prerogatives were exercised by Hugh as regent' (Hugh of Italy page), but the territory is unchanged.

922-925, 296 cells: Provence and Vienne under Louis the Blind, with Hugh of Arles as regent. The shape is unchanged; Cliopatria draws Rudolph II's Italian adventure (922-926) as a separate row, 'Upper Burgundy and Italy'.

correction.text: Louis the Blind's Provence and Lower Burgundy without the Italian kingdom, which he held only 900-902 and briefly in 905

keyframe_review.note: 900-910, 953 cells (243,032 km2): Provence plus 603 Italian cells (a block of northern and central Italy, bbox to 14.8 E and 41.3 N). Louis the Blind was crowned with the Iron Crown at Pavia on 12 October 900 and as emperor in 901, but 'in 902 Berengar defeated Louis's armies and forced him to flee to Provence'; in 905 he was captured at Verona and blinded (21 July) and gave up the Italian crown. Italy is the Kingdom of Italy's land, so the shape is Provence only (Lower Burgundy 896 shape) with the Italian expeditions as contest zones 900-902 and 905 (ledger). Cliopatria keeps Italy until 910; the page ends the claim in 905.

correction.text: Provence and Vienne under Louis the Blind and then Hugh of Arles, without Italy

keyframe_review.note: 926-935, 954 cells (243,470 km2): Provence plus 604 Italian cells. This is Hugh of Arles's realm: 'Berengar's partisans now elected Hugh as king (925)' and in 926 'Hugh crossed the Alps to be crowned'; after Louis the Blind's death (5 June 928) he 'annexed the kingdom to Italy de facto'. Italy belongs to the Kingdom of Italy; the state here is Provence (Lower Burgundy 922 shape) to 930, minus Viennois and Lyonnais from 931 (occupied by Rudolph II) and gone in 933 ('Rudolf abandoned his claims to Italy' in return for Provence). The dossier ends in 933, not 935: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Arles (936) is the union of this land with Upper Burgundy. From 931 the shape is superseded by lower-burgundy_931 (Viennois and Lyonnais ceded to Rudolph II); the dossier ends in 933, so Cliopatria's 934-935 years are outside it.

minus.text: the Viennois and Lyonnais, given to Rudolph II

correction.text: Provence without the Viennois and Lyonnais, which Hugh 'bribed off' Rudolph II with

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 931-933: Hugh of Italy 'bribed off' Rudolph of Burgundy 'with the gift of the Viennois and Lyonnais' in the 931 narrative of the Hugh of Italy page (no month); Provence follows in the treaty of 933 (ledger). The shape is Lower Burgundy 925 minus the Lyonnais and Vienne 60 km (57 cells, 239 left); upper-burgundy_931 (931-932) holds the same 57 cells, so the two dossiers no longer claim them both. It supersedes kingdom-of-lower-burgundy_926 for these years (the orchestrator should confirm the compiler takes the later keyframe).

region.text: Charles of Provence's kingdom: 'Lower Burgundy with Provence' (Cliopatria's 860 shape minus the Lotharingian part it keeps from 866, but with the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble, which Lothair received on his death)

ledger.note: 855: Charles, youngest son of Lothair I, receives Lower Burgundy with Provence. 'By the Treaty of Prüm (19 September 855) his father divided Middle Francia between his three sons'; Charles 'received Lower Burgundy with Provence'; his reign is dated from 23 September 855 (infobox).

region.text: the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble

ledger.note: 863: the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble pass to Lothair. 'Lothair received the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble, to be governed by Girart' when Charles died in January 863.

region.text: Arles, Aix and Embrun (the Provençal provinces)

ledger.note: 863: Arles, Aix and Embrun pass to Louis II. 'Louis received Arles, Aix and Embrun'; with that, 'King Charles of Lower Burgundy died already in 863, and his realm was divided between his brothers' (Lower Burgundy page). The state holds no land until 879.

union.text: the provinces of Arles, Aix, Vienne and Lyon (without Langres), probably Besançon, and the dioceses of Tarentaise, Uzès and Viviers
Mâcon and the northern parts of Boso's realm

region.text: Boso's realm of October 879, with Mâcon and the north that the brothers took in 880

ledger.note: 879: Boso is elected king of Lower Burgundy and Provence. 'They elected Boso king and successor to Louis the Stammerer' at the Synod of Mantaille, 15 October 879; the kingdom 'comprised the ecclesiastical provinces of Arles, Aix, Vienne, and Lyon'. The Lower Burgundy page lists West Francia as the preceding state. The Saône-et-Loire part is the reading of 'They took Mâcon and the northern parts of Boso's realm' (880): the land was Boso's first (lower-burgundy_879 keyframe).

region.text: Mâcon and the northern parts of Boso's realm

ledger.note: 880: Louis III and Carloman II take Mâcon and the north of Boso's realm. 'After Louis and Carloman divided their father's realm at Amiens in March 880, the two brothers joined to march against Boso. They took Mâcon and the northern parts of Boso's realm.' The capture is undated on the page (after March 880), so no month is given; the page names Mâcon only and the region is the Saône-et-Loire reading. Cliopatria's 880 polygon holds 2 of the 35 cells; the lower-burgundy_879 keyframe gives Boso the rest (West Francia's 879 keyframe takes it off West Francia).

region.text: the city of Vienne, Boso's stronghold

ledger.note: 880: the Carolingians besiege Vienne. 'With Charles the Fat, they unsuccessfully besieged Vienne from August to November' (the Charles the Fat page says August to September). The city holds until 882.
882: Vienne falls. 'In August, his brother Richard the Justiciar besieged Vienne again and took it in September' (Boso page); Charles the Fat sent Richard (Charles the Fat page).

region.text: the realm except the county of Vienne

ledger.note: 882: Boso is 'restricted to the county of Vienne'; by 882 he had already lost much of his Burgundian domains. The rest of the realm falls to the Carolingians; the page does not list which counties, so the region is Cliopatria's 880-to-882 reduction.

region.text: Provence and Lower Burgundy as Louis the Blind held them

ledger.note: 887: Charles the Fat confirms the young Louis in Provence. 'In May, Ermengard traveled to Charles' court with Louis, and received confirmation of family estates'; the realm is restored to about its 880 extent. Boso had died in January 887 (Boso page). The page names estates, not counties, so the region is Cliopatria's 887 shape.

region.text: the Lombard kingdom around Pavia and Verona

ledger.note: 900: Louis the Blind invades Italy. 'Louis thus marched his army across the Alps and defeated Berengar' and 'was crowned with the Iron Crown of Lombardy on 12 October 900' at Pavia; emperor in 901. Italy is the Kingdom of Italy's land: it is drawn as contested, not as Lower Burgundy.

region.text: the Lombard kingdom around Pavia and Verona

ledger.note: 902: Berengar drives Louis out. 'In 902 Berengar defeated Louis's armies and forced him to flee to Provence and promise never to return.'

905: Louis breaks his oath and invades Italy again. 'In 905, Louis again invaded Italy but was defeated and blinded for breaking his oath' (Lower Burgundy page); the Louis the Blind page places the capture at Verona.
905: 21 July, Louis is captured at Verona and blinded; he 'was forced to give up his Italian and imperial crowns'. He returns to Vienne.

928: Louis the Blind dies (5 June) and Hugh of Arles takes the crown. 'Louis died in 928 and was succeeded by Hugh' (Lower Burgundy page); 'Hugh annexed the kingdom to Italy de facto' and 'took control of the right to grant fiefs in Provence' (Hugh of Italy page). The Bosonid line ends; the land stays one state until 933.

931: Hugh buys off Rudolph II with Viennois and Lyonnais. 'Lambert's supporters called in Rudolph of Burgundy, whom Hugh bribed off with the gift of the Viennois and Lyonnais' (the page's 931 narrative, no month). New keyframe lower-burgundy_931 removes the land from Lower Burgundy.

region.text: Provence, as the page names it

ledger.note: 933: Hugh gives Provence to Rudolph II. 'He concluded a treaty with Rudolph in 933 by which Rudolf abandoned his claims to Italy' in return for Provence, 'over the heads of Louis the Blind's heirs'.

region.text: the whole realm, absorbed into the Kingdom of Burgundy

ledger.note: 933: Lower Burgundy ends. The page: the realm 'existed from 879 to 933, when it was incorporated into the reunited Kingdom of Burgundy'; 'the two Burgundies were combined' under Rudolph II.

wars.name: Charles the Bald's intervention in Provence
wars.outcome: Charles the Bald 'attempted to intervene in Provence in 861' but 'only reached Macon, being restrained by Hincmar of Rheims'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Carolingian war against Boso
wars.outcome: Louis III and Carloman II take Mâcon and the north after the Amiens division of March 880 (undated); the siege of Vienne (August-November 880, with Charles the Fat) fails; Richard the Justiciar takes Vienne in September 882 and confines Boso to the county of Vienne.
wars.note: The Ribemont page adds: 'Boso suffered several territorial loses, but still kept his kingdom.'

wars.name: Louis the Blind's Italian campaigns

zones.text: the Lombard kingdom around Pavia and Verona

wars.outcome: Louis is crowned King of Italy at Pavia (12 October 900) and emperor (901), is driven out by Berengar in 902, and is captured and blinded at Verona on 21 July 905.

wars.name: Hugh of Italy against Rudolph II of Upper Burgundy
wars.outcome: Hugh 'unsuccessfully attempted to take Burgundy from Rudolph's son, Rudolph II', buys him off with the Viennois and Lyonnais in 931 and cedes Provence in the treaty of 933.
wars.note: The page gives no start year for the attempt; 931 is the dated bribe.

certainty.note: The realm is described by ecclesiastical provinces (Arles, Aix, Vienne, Lyon), not by surveyed lines; the Italian frontier of 900-905 and the Burgundian frontier of 931-933 are approximate.

notes: Merged rows: Cliopatria's 'Lower Burgundy' (860-925) and 'Kingdom of Lower Burgundy' (900-910 and 926-935) share Q33242 and the Wikipedia title 'Lower Burgundy'. They are one state, the Kingdom of Provence / Lower Burgundy, and are reviewed here under the earlier slug; kingdom-of-lower-burgundy gets no dossier of its own. Cliopatria's 860-869 'Lower Burgundy' is two things in one polygon: Charles of Provence's realm (to January 863) and Lothair II's Lotharingia (to 869); the Lotharingian part needs a dossier (kingdom-of-lotharingia, 855-869, counterpart in the West Franks and East Franks ledgers). The state has a gap: it begins at Prüm in September 855, is divided in January 863, and is revived by Boso on 15 October 879; the Lower Burgundy page's infobox dates it only from 879. The dossier starts in 855 because the page itself tells the 855 partition and Cliopatria's first shape is 860. Italian cells: Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Lower Burgundy' shapes carry about 600 Italian cells for 900-910 and 926-935, and Cliopatria has no Kingdom of Italy shape for 900-910 or 922-935; those years need Italy from the kingdom-of-italy dossier (eu-13). Here Italy is drawn as contest zones (900-902, 905), not as Lower Burgundy land. Unsettled: no opened page names a capital before 905 or gives counties for the realm of 855-863; the dates of Hugh's move of the capital to Arles and of Vienne's loss to Charles-Constantine (by 930, Hugh of Italy page) are not given. The infobox of the Lower Burgundy page gives no area, so the Cliopatria areas (71-73 thousand km2 for Provence alone) could not be compared. Repairs of 2026-10-24 after review: (1) Charles of Provence's realm (855-862) now holds the Lyonnais, Vienne and Grenoble (260 cells), which Cliopatria's 866 polygon (Lothair II's kingdom) had taken out. (2) New keyframe lower-burgundy_931 (931-933): the Viennois and Lyonnais leave in 931, so the 57 cells are no longer claimed by upper-burgundy_931 as well. (3) New keyframe lower-burgundy_879 and a 2-cell adjustment of lower-burgundy_880: Saône-et-Loire (Mâcon) is Boso's from October 879 and goes to West Francia after the March 880 Amiens division (month dropped, the capture is undated); West Francia has the mirror keyframe west-franks_879. (4) The 882-886 keyframes keep the county of Vienne although Richard took the city in September 882: the page's 'restricted to the county of Vienne' has no year. (5) Kept as one dossier with the gap of 863-878, as decided by the orchestrator's default: the Lower Burgundy page dates the state from 879 (infobox 'Established: 879') and presents Boso's kingdom as new; the orchestrator may split 855-863 (Charles of Provence's kingdom) into its own dossier. (6) Capital: see identity; Kingdom of Arles page opened, no move dated.
